constraint_decided_it: Nothing in domain/range separated them: P110 (E79->E18), P112 (E80->E18), P111/P113 (E79/E80->E18) and P108 (E12->E24) all hold for an E22 engine and an E22 beam in both answers, and both correctly refuse a second P108 has produced on the engine and reject E81 (whose scope note requires simultaneous destruction and creation with separate identities). What separated them was coverage of the question's second half plus one citation defect: B names the CRM's own direct modification idiom, quoting P31's example verbatim ('The rebuilding of the German Reichstag in Berlin (E11) has modified the Reichstag in Berlin (E24)') and adds P46 is composed of, whose scope note explicitly says E79/E80 are how you document when a component became or ceased to be part of a whole; but B attributes the wording 'replacing a part of an object' to t0056, which the thread does not contain (t0056 records the 2002 Paris decision to add Part Addition/Part Removal, with scope notes about attaching/detaching accessories and components and continuity of identity, never the word replacement).
better_modelling: Neither missed it. The prescribed modelling is: engine as one continuing E22; 1876 E12 Production P108 has produced -> engine; 1932 E80 Part Removal (P112 diminished -> engine, P113 removed -> cast-iron beam) plus E79 Part Addition (P110 augmented -> engine, P111 added -> steel beam), optionally the same activity multiply instantiated; a separate E12 Production P108 has produced -> steel beam by the second firm; and P46 is composed of for the engine/beam part-whole assertion, which only B states.
reasoning: Both answers land on exactly what the CRM prescribes and every property they propose is inside its declared domain and range, so neither is wrong; A's two t1170 quotations and its E11 scope-note quotation on E81 all verify verbatim, and Doerr's 'We definitely regard' / 'We assume identity criteria for E19' make A's framing of it as the CRM's position defensible even though the current E19 scope note does not carry that criterion. B is marked unsupported on the strict rule alone: the quoted phrase 'replacing a part of an object' is not in t0056, although the 2002 Paris-decision provenance it rests on is real. B is nonetheless the better modelling answer because it actually answers the 'more direct way' half of the question with the CRM's own P31 has modified idiom and its verified Reichstag example, and because it asserts P46 is composed of, which P46's scope note ties directly to E79/E80 for precisely this documentation need; A never states the part-whole relation at all.
